q1_issues.issue: The superseded August deadline (TimeAtMost sk_complete_1 (Month august)) is left standing at full strength beside the new October 17 bound on the SAME event symbol, so the KB still asserts a by-August deadline that the sentence explicitly says was extended; nothing marks the first bound as no longer holding.

(Member sk_package_1 medicare_drug_package) fuses the proper noun "Medicare" into a compound kind symbol, which the Compound concepts rules explicitly exclude for proper nouns, and no (Name medicare "Medicare") atom survives anywhere in the parse.

q2_gaps: a stated deadline later revised by the same sentence ("by August, then extended it to Oct. 17") — cessation covers only "no longer / not anymore / used to" for eventualities, and there is no construct for retracting or superseding a time BOUND

an episodic (specific, past) bare-plural subject — "Republicans had pledged" names particular actors, but the determiner rule routes every bare plural to the generic (Inheritance / distributing Implication), which cannot express a one-off past event

a proper-noun modifier inside a three-word common-noun compound ("Medicare drug package") — the compound-kind rule is defined for a two-word modifier_noun and is disapplied for proper nouns, leaving the Name of the proper-noun modifier with nowhere to go
notes: Strong on the parts the instruction set does settle: "pledged to complete" takes the control-verb non-finite pattern (Theme link, subject control copying the group into Agent, no tense of its own), the past perfect correctly emits (Before sk_pledge_1 sk_extend_1) because another asserted event exists to order against, "by August" is correctly a TimeAtMost deadline, and "extended it" treats the occurrence as Patient per the postpone/reschedule rule.
